- question no 34 by mr josé maría gil-robles gil-delgado (h-0079/02): what is the commission's position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer? subject: international adoption of romanian children what is the commission and more particularly its representative in bucharest doing to bring the review of the cases of international adoption of romanian children, which has been blocked for more than nine months by the romanian government, to a rapid conclusion? is the commission aware that this blockage is causing serious damage to hundreds of families in the union who have taken all the necessary steps and paid out considerable sums? what measures does it intend to take to protect the rights of these citizens?
the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. the issue of child protection in romania is one of the most important issues in the cooperation between the commission and romania. it is a subject which i have been actively dealing with since the beginning of my mandate. there can be no doubt that there have been serious problems in romania with regard to the protection of children in state institutions and also with regard to the system of intercountry adoptions. romania has signed the un convention on the rights of the child and also the hague convention on the protection of children. the signatory states to the hague convention have, together with us, often expressed their concern to the romanian government that there are very serious shortcomings in the romanian legislation and in the romanian practice of adoption and implementation. i have to tell you, mr president, that i have had to convince myself that in romania commercial child trafficking - and this is about the worst thing there is - has been very common, that on the other hand, of course, adoptions were also carried out in a completely proper manner, and that there was a large grey area between commercial child trafficking and normal international adoptions. the commission has therefore been working hard with the romanian government to bring about a complete change in the whole system, from the legislation to the institutions, the structures, the procedures, the decision-making processes, everything. nothing in the system we had in romania regarding international adoptions could stay the way it is. in order to ensure that during this period of reform of the system there is no abuse of children, the commission has strongly advocated a moratorium on intercountry adoptions. i am very happy that the current romanian government has succeeded in enforcing this moratorium. it is not the commission's policy to prevent international adoptions from taking place. quite the opposite! it is the commission's policy to help ensure that these international adoptions take place in a system which is fully transparent, follows clear internationally recognised rules and ensures that there is no possibility of child abuse in any case. i hope that in a not too distant future the appropriate legal and administrative conditions will have been created in romania so that the normal systems of intercountry adoption can be restored. the cases to which you refer in your question, mr president, which have already been initiated but were not yet decided when the moratorium was imposed, are being examined by the romanian government on a case-by-case basis and if it is absolutely clear that there are no problems with this adoption, the romanian government has the possibility of breaking the moratorium in these cases. i think that's going to help solve the problem you've described. i would like to say again very clearly, mr president, even though this may not be welcome everywhere: when weighing the needs of romanian children and the needs of parents in any country who would like to adopt a child, our first concern must always be the protection of children. i think it's more reasonable to tell families who want to adopt a child that they have to wait a few months than to risk the corrupt practices that we've had in this country in child welfare being carried on in just one case.

question no 51 by mr esko olavi seppänen (h-0083/02) subject: disarmament of fishing vessels in preparing the 2002 budget, appropriations were allocated for the disarmament of the fishing fleets of member states to compensate for the lack of renewal of the fisheries agreement with morocco. on what criteria does the commission base its granting of these appropriations? can we benefit from this if, instead of actually disarming them, we sell the ships in question to the moroccans, for example? is it possible to provide funds for the disarming of ships built with other community aid?
the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. on 17 december last year the council adopted the commission proposal to enable fishermen and ship owners operating under the fisheries agreement with morocco to restructure their fleet and their fishing activities by means of appropriate financial support. the budget for this action is eur 197 million. of this, €170 million is in this year's budget and €27 million is to be provided in next year's budget. the appropriations shall be used as follows: at least 40% of the funds must be used for the scrapping or final conversion of vessels for purposes other than fishing. a maximum of 28% of the appropriations may be used for the final transfer of vessels to a third country, including in the context of a joint venture, or for the modernisation of vessels. the commission has also proposed that at least 32% of the funds be used for socioeconomic measures, such as retraining programmes for fishermen who have lost their jobs or early retirement schemes. it follows that the permanent transfer of vessels to morocco can also be promoted by selling or by setting up a joint venture in morocco. however, the premium for the formation of such a joint venture is only 80% of the scrapping premium and the premium for the export of a vehicle is only 50% of the scrapping premium. in addition, a shipowner who has bought his vessel with a community aid and now wishes to export it with a subsidy or transfer it to a mixed company must repay part of the aid received for the purchase. the amount to be reimbursed depends on the age of the vessel. for example, for a five-year-old ship, at least half of the aid still has to be repaid.
the commission is not prepared to accept this. it is quite clear that this programme is a specific programme adopted to meet the particular difficulties arising from the non-existence of the morocco agreement. the conditions i have mentioned also apply to this specific programme. the only exception to this programme is the structural funds for fisheries, which apply to all scrapping operations and where the same conditions apply everywhere. only in this particular case will this additional money make possible the demolition and sale of the buildings on these improved conditions.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not undermined by the current crisis. - mr president, agriculture is an economic activity which depends on biological processes and which manages a large part of the community's natural resources. for this reason, it must play a central role in the conservation of biodiversity in two ways: first, by consolidating environmentally compatible agricultural practices and, secondly, by ensuring the survival of viable farms and production systems throughout the european union. the unlimited intensification of agriculture is as bad for biodiversity as the cessation of farmers' activity and the consequent decline of rural areas. a community strategy for biodiversity must ensure sustainable agriculture in its broadest sense, which, in addition to the biological aspects, includes economic and social requirements and, in short, the survival of the rural environment. the maintenance of this sustainable agriculture is also an imperative of the european agricultural model, based on the defence of agricultural multifunctionality, as has been reiterated in the council and in the european parliament in numerous resolutions. the cap is a useful instrument for biodiversity, as are the earth summit resolutions adopted at the helsinki and gothenburg councils. it is therefore wrong to confine the defence of biodiversity to the strict limits of the second pillar of the community's agricultural policy - and more specifically to environmental programmes to promote the extension of organic farming, the preservation of indigenous breeds and the protection of the various natural habitats, etc. - for two reasons: firstly, because the second pillar of the cap represents 10% of the agricultural budget and, secondly, because agri-environmental programmes, although covering 20% of the agricultural area, have been applied very unevenly and are now practically limited to the least productive areas of five member states of the union, a situation aggravated by the weak framework attributed to the eco-conditionality of aid, namely markets which have resulted in the formulation of a minimum. we should therefore extend cross compliance and encourage more active competition between the mechanisms of agricultural market policy in favour of the environment and biodiversity. we must support these demands in legislation on food quality, plant protection products, seeds and genetic resources. it is urgent that we strengthen the second pillar of the cap from the financial point of view, and that we differentiate between measures for socio-rural development and measures for the agro-environment. we have a major challenge to face: consolidating the community's agricultural policies and bringing them together so that they work in parallel to conserve biodiversity.
- mr president, we agree with mrs béguin's report because it is based on a reality: neither the convention on biological diversity, signed in 1992, nor the various international conventions, nor community law, in particular the birds and habitats directives, have succeeded in halting the deterioration of biodiversity. it also clearly recalls that thousands of species that have not even been identified are going to disappear. in fact, 11,000 species of fauna and flora are threatened with extinction. i think that's enough to make the appropriate action. the rapporteur welcomes the proposed plans but points out that there are plans which have not yet been implemented, such as the one relating to forests. and it speaks clearly of the need to integrate environmental policy into the rest of agricultural, fisheries and other policies. i have little time, mr president, so i will give you an example, because the examples express better than anything what should be done: the use of eaggf funds to destroy the last remaining laurel forest on the island of gran canaria. this weekend i was on the island of gran canaria with a group of local people who complained to the european commission - - mr president-in-office of the council, mr president, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, an event of the historical significance of enlargement can only be tackled from a very broad consensus. i would like to stress here that a financial consensus must be reached. in recent years, the european union has been operating through a multiannual agreement, which is embodied in the so-called financial perspective and which has made it possible to achieve, through this consensus, two fundamental things: interinstitutional peace - which is very necessary for the preparation of an annual budget - and multiannual financial programming, which is a very useful instrument of budgetary policy. we all remember the difficulties with which the last financial perspective was agreed in berlin in 1999, which is valid until 2006, and we are all aware of the extraordinary difficulties that will arise in negotiating a new financial perspective until 2013, with new actors in this parliament and with the new member states already in the council, two budgetary authorities that will be faced with very new circumstances. among other variables, the new financial consensus will necessarily take into account the impact of a reformed common agricultural policy, real convergence in the current objective 1 areas - which will be affected by the statistical effect - and the absorption capacity of the new member states; a new decision on own resources and their ceiling - now set at 1.24% - will also be necessary, which will have to be ratified by the member states. in short, perhaps the negotiation of a new financial perspective should not begin until there is a certainty of full agreement between all the parties. if the present financial framework can cope with enlargement, we should perhaps extend its life until we have a comprehensive assessment of the new financial situation.
- mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as regards the framework for transatlantic relations, i believe that we must start from the current framework, which is the madrid declaration of december 1995, made under the spanish presidency. i do not recall the president-in-office of the council mentioning this declaration, which defines our framework; what is not sensible is that we have to pay for this when in this parliament we have to deal systematically with the banana war, hormones and gmos, and we always have to see in the list which retaliatory measures are appropriate for our constituency in our country. our american friends and allies must understand that this is not the way to work and that is why we are asking the commission to take the strongest possible line to bring them to their senses.

- (es) nothing can justify the violation of the fundamental rights and freedoms of the person which derive from his inalienable dignity. i therefore oppose fundamentalism as an expression of a thought which denies the freedom of the individual, whether male or female, and his right to choose his own path, and i consider that the european union must defend and promote, by all the means at its disposal, respect for human rights wherever they are violated. but i cannot accept the izquierdo report's condemnation of religious values and religious fact, which is hidden behind the condemnation of fundamentalism, and not only in relation to christianity. it is one thing to have freedom of religious belief which is compatible with respect for human rights, but it is quite another to impose standards of conduct which involve the deprivation of human dignity and the violation of these rights. it is one thing to defend the separation of church and state, a view which i fully share because it is the basis of the democratic system, but it is quite another to deny, in the name of secularism, the right of the church and religious communities to freedom of expression, that is to say, the right to interpret, in the light of their own thinking, the facts of public and political life which govern the lives of citizens. today, by approving this report, the european parliament has done a small favour to the cause of the freedoms we want to promote, because in addition to condemning fundamentalism, there is in fact a new form of fundamentalism that they want to impose on us: secular fundamentalism, which is to be condemned in the same way as any other fundamentalism, insofar as everyone denies the freedom of everyone by choosing his own model of life. i shall now explain why i voted against this report.
- mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, the transatlantic relationship is very important: it was a priority of the previous spanish presidency, it is a priority of the present one and we must therefore do everything in our power to preserve it. the point is that, like all relationships, it is a two-way street, and we are now noticing that the bush administration has great temptations to act on its own; that is, to practice the frank sinatra doctrine, i'll do it my way, both politically - i have only two minutes and i cannot go on - and commercially. the trade was never a factor that tested this relationship; we considered trade disputes to be the exception while trade benefits were the rule; the fact is that now they have gone too far, both in the case of steel and in the case of another product that is less talked about, namely clementines. the situation is different: clementines affect only one country, and indeed the region from which commissioner solbes comes, and steel affects us all. both cases are against wto rules without any justification and, moreover, are self-punishment by the united states. we must deal with indirect damage - i think we can take action on traffic diversions - as well as direct damage. there are several possibilities: one is to act in the wto, but it will take time and in the long run we will all be dead; there is also the possibility of laissez-faire, that is to say, doing nothing, because the downstream industries which import steel inputs will become less competitive and we will therefore be able to replace them; but what i think we have to do is to act immediately. the interim measures that can be taken are at hand, under the judgment of the 'panel' on the foreign sales task corporation and therefore we must act immediately.
- mr president, mr commissioner, mr president-in-office of the council, in a well-known passage from julius caesar we read a sentence which says: 'good or evil is not in the stars, dear brutus, but in us who are below them'. the quote seems particularly appropriate at this moment, because the gravity of the problem lies not so much in the protectionist measures affecting the united states as in the reaction which the european union must have to these commercial aggressions, relations in which the steel and clementine issue - - madam president, the regulation of the stock market must achieve the reconciliation of two objectives: firstly, to give european companies more opportunities to obtain money at a lower price, and secondly, to protect investors. i believe that this reconciliation has been achieved in the report on market abuse and has also been achieved, thanks to some transactional amendments to the directive regulating the supervision or control of financial conglomerates. unfortunately, i see three attacks on the principle of legal protection in mr huhne's report: those concerning the definition of a public offer, those concerning the choice of the authority responsible for monitoring the prospectus and, thirdly, those concerning the exclusion of small and mediumsized enterprises from the obligation to provide information. i'll go in pieces. in the definition of a public offer the rapporteur proposes that this information be provided to the investor at the last stage, at the stage immediately preceding the conclusion of the contract. in my view, this information should be made available and publicly available from the moment the investor is asked for money and it is obvious that my formula, which coincides with that of the commission, does not preclude that this survey should analyse the possibilities of investment with professional investors. secondly, as regards the completely free choice of the supervisory authority which you propose, i, who was in my previous incarnation a financial inspector, do not think it is a good idea for taxpayers to be able to choose their financial inspector and i do not think it is a good idea for financial institutions to be able to choose the ultimate supervisory body. i think that the formula proposed by the commission is more consistent, more respectful of the previous directives, more consistent with common sense - the national authority knows best what the applicable national law is, which it has to inform the investor about - and, above all, offers less risk, because the formula of absolute freedom, in my view, opens up competition, a race between supervisory authorities to lower the bar and attract investors which would undermine legal certainty. on the last point, concerning small and mediumsized enterprises, i cannot agree with the rapporteur in excluding small and mediumsized enterprises, especially since small and mediumsized enterprises have a capital of 350 million pesetas, which would mean excluding 80% of the companies listed on the stock exchange. i am sorry that i cannot finish; i shall conclude the dialogue with mr huhne, now by letter and hopefully later orally.
the rapporteur. - madam president, to assess the importance of this debate, i would like to begin by recalling the remote origin of this proposal for a directive. the origins of this system can be traced back to 1988, to the directive on the liberalization of capital movements of 24 june of that year. the authors of the directive were aware of the opportunities which this liberalization opened up for the avoidance of national taxes on capital gains by placing the investment in a country other than the investor's country of residence. in short, we can say that the risk was and still is that each member state, each country within the single market which was being formed and which is now formed, would act as a tax haven for the other member states. this risk, as i said, was warned by the authors of the directive on the liberalization of capital movements, who asked the commission and the council to legislate on this point, on the fiscal aspect of the liberalization of capital movements within one year, that is, in 1989. the commission put forward its proposal in time - mrs scrivener was the commissioner at the time - but this proposal, which basically consisted in introducing a withholding tax for payments to residents of another member state, was not accepted by the council and was rejected, becoming practically a kind of legislative abortion. in 1997, as part of the so-called monti package, the commission made a new proposal based on the model of coexistence on which parliament had to draw up a report but which was not finally unanimously agreed by the council. the next step is the santa maria de feira agreement, in which the european council - that is, the heads of state or government - having accepted a proposal from the ecofin council, reached a principle of political agreement on the basis of the points i shall mention below. first, the member states would undertake to establish a system for exchanging information on interest payments to residents of another member state, which means that this would entail the lifting of banking secrecy. secondly, as an exceptional and transitional system, it is permissible for certain states, in particular belgium, austria and luxembourg, to apply a system of withholding tax instead of the exchange of information, i.e. instead of lifting banking secrecy. finally, the implementation of this entire legal framework was and remains subject to negotiations with third countries (switzerland, the united states, andorra and others) for the application of equivalent measures and to the application of the same measures by the member states in the territories under their control (the channel islands and others). our assessment of the proposal for a directive which reflects these feira guidelines is entirely positive. we believe that this is broadly in line with the approach advocated by the oecd, which is currently the most active forum for discussion in this area. the essential problem, and i shall conclude with this, madam president, in this whole scheme is - and nobody escapes it - that of negotiations with third countries. in short, the problem is how to get the swiss confederation to agree to lift banking secrecy. but even at the risk of appearing naive and optimistic, i would like to warn that everything in this life is subject to change and that not even swiss banking secrecy is what it used to be. i would like to draw attention to the following fact: the united states has succeeded in imposing a regulation, the so-called qualified intermediary agreement, by means of internal legislation, under which swiss banks and those of other countries are obliged to report to the internal revenue service the returns received by a us customer - a us person - from an equally us asset, to lift the banking secrecy in relation to these payments or to apply a 30% withholding tax. it is not lost on anyone that this regulation can be circumvented simply by investing in a non-u.s. asset. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud, and it is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the financial interests of the union. the european union and the united states must therefore show what concerted action can achieve in this area. we believe that this is the way to go in negotiations with the united states and other countries. we are confident, and i conclude with this, madam president, that the commission will be able to conduct the negotiations with a good heart to find a solution to this problem of taxation of savings, which, to be honest, should have been solved a long time ago.
the rapporteur. - madam president, at this point any misunderstanding is possible. if a polling company were to ask people whether the european union has its own personality, i have the impression that the answer would be overwhelmingly in the affirmative. and yet, such a response by the citizens would be wrong, clearly wrong, but it would demonstrate at least three things: firstly, the opacity of the current situation in which the institutional architecture of the european union lives; secondly, the lack of information to the citizens by the governments on issues such as the one we are dealing with and, undoubtedly the most important, that the reality is ahead of the decisions taken so far by the intergovernmental conferences. the citizens believe that the european union has its own personality, and yet the governments at these conferences have refused to give it their own. the european union has existed since the maastricht treaty - and for some years now - but it has never been given legal personality, either then or since; the last example was the treaty of nice. the question is why have governments refused to do so to date? in this sense, she is still a minor living under the legal authority of her parents: the european communities. the question i ask is: can we continue this contradictory, little-understood situation any longer? the answer is clear: no, because the current situation creates legal confusion, political confusion, international and internal confusion, institutional confusion and, above all, as i said at the beginning of this speech, confusion among citizens. let me give three examples from the international point of view: one can travel to a country like equatorial guinea and see that the commission delegation there is from the commission of the european communities and not from the european union; one can listen to the representative we have at the united nations and find that he is from the european communities and not from the union; or one can even see with satisfaction that there is a commitment on the part of a united europe to sign the kyoto protocol in a very short time and realize that it is not the european union but the european communities that are going to sign it. this report also coincides with the start of the convention on the future of europe, which this parliament wants to be constitutional. it will therefore be our first contribution to the convention after its opening. and it is logical that it also occupies the same thematic space. we want the convention, and then the intergovernmental conference, to address the question of giving the union legal personality, and this would have undoubted advantages: legal clarity, the first of these; the second, better perception and action of the union at international level; the third, to be an indispensable element for the implementation of a system of protection of fundamental rights at union level; the fourth, to contribute to the visibility of political union and facilitate the identification of the citizen with the european union itself and, the fifth, to contribute to the correction of the dysfunctions caused by the system of pillars. but we also believe that legal personality is necessary to complete political union and that the process of constitutionalising the union also requires that it should have its own legal personality. it is a necessary condition for achieving these objectives in a coherent way. if that were not the case, what would be the subject of the future constitutional text, what would be the protagonist of a european constitution, the union, the communities - one of which is due to die next summer - ? that is why we are calling for the union to be given legal personality in the future european constitution. we asked for this in the report of the committee on constitutional affairs, of which i am the rapporteur, in conjunction with the opinions of the committees on foreign affairs, human rights, common security and defence policy and legal affairs and internal market, which i would like to regard as very positive contributions. i believe that this coincidence in calling for the union to have legal personality extends to the last two presidencies of the council, as both belgium and spain have said. this, madam president, is not a matter for legal experts, but a point that is very understandable to any citizen: to know that you are a citizen of a union with its own personality, which you can and must govern democratically, with transparency, and demand that your responsibilities are met.
- mr president, the excellent report by marie-arlette carlotti is both an optimistic statement of confidence in the potential of the cotonou agreement and a call for everyone to take responsibility so that this potential does not remain a lost opportunity and is realized even in its most ambitious consequences. the report stresses that cotonou represents a significant step in the process of cooperation between the european union and a growing number of african, caribbean and pacific states, which has been in place for decades, with a view to promoting their development. we are thus reminded that we are facing a process which is coming of age here and also adapting to the present times. the new agreement was not given to our partners by the europeans, but was long and rigorously negotiated with them. we are therefore faced with an agreement which is an association between partners who are equal in respect, recognition and rights. the agreement, together with its economic and trade component, introduces an innovative political dimension which should make it possible for an acp-eu community united around the proclaimed democratic values and with a very great capacity for influence to emerge on the international scene in the pursuit of a world of justice, balance, freedom, law, peace and prosperity, fairly distributed and shared. but all the confidence expressed in the report is in turn conditional on the responsibility of everyone to take advantage of what is provided for in the agreement. the rapporteur therefore calls, first of all, on the member states of the union for whom ratification of the cotonou agreement is not a priority. the european parliament itself is also called upon to devote the attention it deserves to the follow-up to the cotonou agreement. the responsibility of those members who participate as representatives of parliament in the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly. we are called upon to make this assembly truly parliamentary the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not affected by the crisis. i would also like to recall the parliament's strong institutional support for the nut and carob sector, which is reflected in numerous resolutions which show the importance of this sector in the union. in july 2001, the commissioner, mr fischler, told the council of agriculture ministers that a detailed study of the community dried fruit sector would be carried out and that, if necessary, concrete proposals for action in its favour would be made, providing a solution to the improvement plans expiring in 2001. in this context, the commission has presented a new extension of the improvement plans for one year, which i have welcomed, but i would like to note that this is only the last transitional instrument until we have a definitive proposal, which ensures the continuity of the sector and solves the difficult situation and uncertainty facing producers in the european union. the need to tackle definitive support measures once and for all is the primary objective of our report. the dried fruit sector is of great importance in the union from a social, economic and environmental point of view. the crop has more than one million hectares spread over the mediterranean countries, mostly in very disadvantaged areas with difficult agronomic conditions: drylands, sloping crops, etc. the difficulties these products face in remaining on the market and being an economically viable activity without direct support from the public authorities are therefore great, aggravated by the strong competition from abroad, from hazelnuts from turkey and from almonds from the united states, products which are developed under production conditions not comparable to those in europe and which are covered by tariff concessions through international agreements. the dried fruit sector is an example of multifunctionality and is absolutely necessary for the socioeconomic maintenance of many families in rural areas of the union, for the objectives it fulfils in terms of land use planning - there being no other alternative production - and for the environmental functions it performs in terms of erosion, firefighting and the safeguarding of native genetic material, and which, on the other hand, has exceptional organoleptic characteristics. in view of this difficult situation and the lack of competitiveness, the council adopted in 1989 a series of specific measures whose main objective was to contribute to improving the quality of products and their competitiveness. the 10-year improvement plans, which expired in 2000, were extended until 15 june 2001. the achievements of these plans have therefore been positive, with significant improvements in production and marketing. but the objective of improving competitiveness has not been achieved, given the difficult structural starting conditions. the current commission proposal provides for a further extension of these last plans until 15 june 2002 with a reduction in the community contribution from 82% to 75%. as regards hazelnuts in particular, the aid per kilo is maintained for the 2001/02 harvest but is granted only to farmers belonging to producer organisations which do not benefit from the extension. the committee on agriculture and rural development has therefore sought to make a substantial improvement on the commission's proposal by its amendment. as regards the conditions for the aid for hazelnuts, it is unacceptable to exclude from the payment of the aid producer organisations wishing to benefit from the extension of the improvement plans. this treatment of aid to some producer organisations only as compared with others is discriminatory and would place them in a situation of unfair competition. as regards the level of national co-financing, the proposed increase for the extended plans over those in force is unjustified. in this context, the percentage for nuts is very modest and does not explain this proposal at all. as regards the areas covered by the eligible plans, the aid should be extended taking into account the area certified in the plans of the last year and not the area for which aid has been applied for. the committee on agriculture and rural development has considered that, in order to improve knowledge and control of production, it is necessary to establish measures for the implementation of a geographical information system. the committee on agriculture has also noted the need to establish a definitive framework for aid to the sector, calling for permanent support in the form of aid per hectare to ensure that producers' incomes are maintained in a sustainable farming situation. hence the need to link this last extension with the definitive aid, the ultimate aim being to consolidate a permanent aid scheme channelled through producer organisations. i do not want to end without recalling the specific review by the committee on agriculture of the inclusion of chestnut in the dried fruit sector. the environmental and protection aspects of a very important ecosystem in clear decline go beyond protecting this tree and its fruit linked to forest areas and ancestral pastoral cultures. finally, i would point out that two identical amendments have been tabled in the house, aimed at increasing the aid for hazelnuts by one additional marketing year. i cannot support these amendments, although i understand and share the difficult market situation that hazelnuts are currently experiencing. when applying for a definitive scheme, the hazelnut aid will then be covered by that scheme and it is therefore not appropriate to prolong any longer a temporary situation with an expiry date which has only generated uncertainty. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that we can continue to consume the best desserts, the best turrón, and the products made from the best and most tasty hazelnuts and almonds in the world.

strategy for sustainable development. the orientation towards the phasing-out of tobacco subsidies is determined by the need to ensure a high level of human health protection in all community policies, in accordance with article 152 of the treaty. we also know that there is no direct link between tobacco production and the amount of tobacco smoked, which means that less tobacco is smoked if we support less tobacco farming. the political issue is article 152, which clearly states that all community policies, including any supporting policies, must guarantee a high level of protection of human health. so the other question no longer arises. the deletion of this recital proposed in amendment no 2 cannot therefore be accepted. the reference to parliament's resolution proposed in amendment no 3 cannot be accepted either, since it is not relevant to the rationale of the proposed regulation. amendments nos 4 to 6, which call for an analysis of the socioeconomic impact, are - mr president, i believe that programmes of administrative cooperation in immigration policy and related matters are of great importance. today we are discussing the argo programme, the ultimate aim of which is to ensure that third-country nationals are treated equally. i would also like to point out that in the areas covered in whole or in part by this programme, the number of directives, regulations and other instruments in force or under way is very high, and that this acquis communautaire must be applied in a consistent manner, guaranteeing equally the rights of third country nationals. there are very important aspects which the programme should take into account: it is essential that measures are taken to prevent illegal immigration, to combat document forgery and to take action in the field of consular cooperation. the objective of establishing a common policy in this area is a great challenge and its success depends to a large extent on the union being a genuine area of security and freedom. my country has in a few years gone from being a country of emigration to a country which receives a large number of immigrants and which at the same time has problems arising from its situation at the external border of the union. while this is not new - - mr president, commissioner, with the creation of the european aviation safety agency the european union aims to achieve and maintain a high level of safety and environmental protection, which is in the objective interest of european society and also of the construction of the union. we are naturally in agreement with this purpose. i would like to say, however, that safety and environmental protection have a lot to do with the airport structure, which is being seriously undermined by the tendency to centralize airports which prevails in most european countries and is promoted by central governments which, for political and power reasons, concentrate investments in capital, and by the so-called flag carriers which, for the same reasons, centralize their flights at the same airports. as a result, most of europe, as in my own country, galicia, suffers serious damage from lack of good air links, traffic is concentrated on the air corridors linking the capitals, and the people living near these central airports suffer the consequences of noise and congestion. all this is contrary to the sustainable development which we must pursue from the point of view of security, as well as economic, social and environmental aspects. i think we are therefore faced with a serious problem which we must begin to solve.

commission. – mr president, as mentioned in the question put by mr brok, the commission communication of december 1997, 'implementing the strategy of the union's defence-related industries', regulated an ambitious overall approach. it contained a draft council common position relating to the development of a european armaments policy and an action plan of 14 points for the defence-related industries. among the 14 items of the action plan, some of these measures require legislation, while others can be carried out using instruments already available to the union. a good deal of progress has been made with regard to most of the actions, in fact with 11 out of a total of 14. however, until recently, council discussions have generally been characterised by differences of opinion between the member states preventing the adoption of a common position on the framing of a european armaments policy. this made progress especially difficult with regard to measures requiring legislative action such as the action plan items on customs duties and intra-community transfers. i would like to underline today, however, that the commission has begun infringement proceedings against 10 member states on the question of the proper application of the common customs tariff on military and non-military goods. this action may serve to reactivate discussions on the issue. furthermore, as regards the intra-community transfers of these goods, work on trying to find appropriate technical solutions continues and some progress has been made. despite the difficulties in moving forward on some of these critical issues as rapidly as we had hoped, i would like to stress that the analysis advocating a need for re-structuring the european defence industry and for creating a single market for defence products is as valid as ever. it is even more pertinent for at least two reasons. they are: firstly, the development of the european security policy and defence policy and secondly, the constitution of trans-national defence companies. the competitiveness of the european defence industry is vital to the credibility of the nascent european security and defence policy. thus, the commission expects that governments increasingly recognise the urgency for a change in attitudes in order to end policies and practices that prevent european defence companies from working together more efficiently. such a change in the position of the member states might allow the commission to contribute more effectively to the creation of the european defence equipment market through exercising its competence, and to community policies such as the creation of the single market in defence, external trade etc. thus, the commission intends – and that was the question to which i replied positively, mr brok – to re-examine and update the action plan in order to take into account any new developments. in addition the commission is pursuing the objective of promoting the greater competitiveness of europe's defence industry in close cooperation with national authorities and industry representatives. mr brok also mentioned the question of standardisation. an important initiative in this context is our efforts aimed at promoting awareness of the importance of standardisation issues for the efficiency and the competitiveness of the european defence industries, and of investigating options and possible start-up actions for defence standards reform. on this occasion, the european standardisation organisation cen was identified as the ideal forum to implement this effort in the form of a handbook of defence standards and procedures which, when in place, will offer more transparency, improving inter-operability, harmonisation requirements and cost-efficiency in procurement. in the foreseeable future, two ongoing processes make us feel confident that efficient solutions may finally be within reach. they are: progress on esdp paving the way for harmonising the demand in europe for defence equipment and, in parallel, the gradual recognition of the need to harmonise the rules and regulations which affect the competitiveness of the industries once restructured. as commissioner patten mentioned, these developments are acknowledged in the star 21 initiative: the strategic aerospace review for 21st century currently in progress. star 21 aims to broaden the understanding of aerospace-related issues in europe and trigger the action which will ensure that europe's aerospace industry can play a full part in europe's future. this initiative brings together senior representatives from industry with the commission, the council and also with the european parliament as was mentioned here today, with the participation of mr von wogau and of mr westendorp y cabeza, chairman of the committee on industry. i hope that this report, which we will present in july, will give a further push to our efforts to have a strong competitive european defence industry.

situation in the middle east is critical. the palestinian territories are on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe. the palestinian authority faces uncertainty about its future and stability and security in the region are clearly in jeopardy. all attempts to defuse the crisis have so far failed and have not prevented the violence from escalating in recent weeks. a spiral of violence generated by brutal terrorist attacks by palestinian suicide bombers and by the resulting israeli reprisals is leading to greater suffering for both peoples every day. once again, it must be reiterated that the conflict we face will not be resolved until the palestinians are free from the 1967 occupation and the israelis feel at peace and in security; until the israelis and palestinians can live in two states, with secure and internationally recognized borders. and once again, it is also necessary to insist that there is no military solution to this conflict and that peace and security can only be achieved through negotiations. the international community, and more specifically the european union, has a responsibility and a role that cannot be denied. it is also necessary that any intervention or initiative be rigorously coordinated, especially between the united nations, the european union and the major powers involved. the union presidency has not been idle in these last weeks. in the barcelona declaration of 16 march last, the european union stressed the need to address all aspects, both security, political and economic. the declaration also reiterated the basis for a settlement of the conflict, namely un security council resolutions 242, 338 and 1397 and the principles of the madrid and oslo conferences and subsequent agreements which would enable the two states, israel and palestine, to live in peace and security. the objective - as i said earlier - is twofold: the creation of a democratic, viable and independent palestinian state, ending the occupation of 1967, and the guarantee to israel of the right to live within secure borders, guaranteed by the commitment of the international community and, in particular, of the arab countries. the latest phase of the present crisis coincided almost in time with the end of the arab league summit in beirut. the union presidency, represented by the spanish prime minister, attended the summit to show the european union's interest in the whole process and to support the saudi initiative, which would have meant the possibility of normalizing relations between israel and its arab neighbours in return for israeli withdrawal to the 1967 lines and a just solution to the refugee problem on the basis of the relevant un resolutions. it was the first time that a representative of the european union had attended a summit of the arab league at the highest level. the european union has made unremitting efforts to achieve an immediate ceasefire, the withdrawal of israeli troops from palestinian towns, the restoration of full freedom of movement for president arafat, compliance with international law and the return to political negotiations. we have also unequivocally condemned terrorist acts, such as the attack on netanya, and we have appealed to arafat to take all necessary measures to prevent them. the right of israel to fight terrorism cannot limit the operational effectiveness of president arafat as the legitimate representative of the palestinian people and the palestinian national authority. the union calls for an end to the attacks on the pa headquarters in ramallah and for the immediate withdrawal of the israeli army from the city. the resolution of the arab league summit in beirut provides a solid basis for moving towards a political perspective for a just and comprehensive solution in the region and for the normalization of relations between israel and the arab world. the presidency's diplomatic contacts at all political levels with the other european capitals, with all the arab countries in the region, as well as with the united states and russia, are aimed at imposing the necessary coordination among all the international actors to stop the conflict and start the solution of the crisis. recently, given the gravity of the situation, the presidency of the union summoned the israeli ambassador to convey four points to him: firstly, there is no military solution to the conflict; secondly, israeli troops must withdraw from palestinian towns as provided for in resolution 1402, which must be implemented immediately, and the siege on president arafat must end; thirdly, israel must allow the special envoys to carry out their diplomatic mission and have free access to president arafat; fourthly, israel must guarantee free access for the european union's diplomatic and consular representatives to its nationals and guarantee them the normal discharge of their diplomatic and consular duties. as president-in-office of the council of the european union, spain convened an extraordinary general affairs council of the european union on 3 april in luxembourg with a triple objective: to coordinate the actions of the member states of the union, to express the union's presidency's concern about developments and its will not to remain passive in an intolerable situation, and to exert the full political weight of the european union in an action aimed at unlocking the current situation. as a result of this meeting, as you know, it was decided to send the presidency and the high representative, mr solana, to the area with the aim of meeting the parties at the highest level, to demand an immediate ceasefire, the implementation of un resolutions 1397 and 1402 and a return to negotiations on a political agreement. the opposition convinced, as it is also convinced that president bush's speech last thursday constitutes a new attempt to restore the terms of the conflict and to seek a short-term solution. the european union considers that further steps should be directed towards the following objectives: full and immediate implementation of security council resolution 1402; urgent need for a genuine ceasefire and commission. – mr president, i should like to say at the outset how strongly i endorse what has been said by the high representative and by the presidency of the council. how have we come to this? almost ten years ago israel and the palestinians laid the foundation for a peaceful settlement of the arab/israeli conflict by recognising each other's right to exist and by concluding the oslo accord which helped to establish a palestinian governmental structure for the first time ever. it equally helped israel to improve its diplomatic and economic standing in the international community. the oslo agreement also offered a precise time-line, at the end of which, in 1999, we should have been able to witness the final israeli/palestinian peace agreement. alas, the promise of oslo has not been delivered, partly because of what has happened on the israeli side, with the rapid expansion of settlements and the non-implementation of agreed withdrawals from areas in the west bank, and partly because of palestinian violence perpetrated by extremist forces with the clear aim of sabotaging any palestinian/israeli peace deal. subsequently, the meeting in camp david in the summer of 2000 and the last-ditch attempts to find a negotiated solution at taba in january 2001 also failed to bring a lasting peace. since then we have seen appalling destruction and misery. israel – a democratic state that rightly takes pride in its democracy, rule of law and humanitarian principles, and which undeniably is threatened by horrendous suicide bombings – has, i fear, behaved in a way which contradicts much that it stands for. the commission - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that those of us who are concerned about maritime safety and the protection of our seas - and, of course, within maritime safety we put the protection of crews first - are today witnessing the culmination of yet another measure within the erika i and erika ii packages, which is a set of measures that are providing the european union with sufficient and appropriate instruments to carry out real action to prevent and avoid accidents at sea. the erika disaster reminded the world of the continuing risk of shipping petroleum products and highlighted the need for better knowledge and monitoring of maritime traffic between european coasts. the measures we have proposed in the commission have gone much further and have not been limited to proposals for the oil sector but have been extended to maritime traffic in general. today's proposal for a directive on maritime traffic monitoring responds to that concern. it provides for a comprehensive strategy to ensure a high level of safety of traffic along european coasts and its objective - i repeat - is prevention, through more precise identification and increased surveillance of vessels. it also aims to improve the response of the coastal authorities in the event of an accident or risk of an accident, since, as mr hatzidakis said, port control, the establishment of safe havens and assistance to ships in difficulty are absolutely key elements. i would like to say that throughout the analysis and discussion of this proposal, the commission has had the active support of parliament, both in this and in previous proposals, and most especially the constructive input of the rapporteur, mr sterckx. i believe that the cooperation between the two institutions has borne fruit and that we are very close today to reaching a final agreement on a text which, from the outset, was not free from sensitive issues, such as the prohibition of going to sea in case of bad weather or the same ports of refuge, to which i referred a moment ago, or also the obligation to carry transponders or black boxes. in this connection, i would once again like to commend mr watts for his tenacity, which has made it possible for the council to reach agreement since the conciliation on the port state control directive. i would like to say that compensation for damage that may be caused by the ports of refuge is a basic element - and i agree with what mr jarzembowski has said - in getting the member states of the union to make ports of refuge available, which is an absolutely key issue. ladies and gentlemen, i would like to conclude by thanking again the rapporteur, mr sterckx, and all the committee members for the excellent work they have done. we share many of your concerns and we will accept all the amendments put forward. in this connection, i would like to mention the follow-up to the report after three years and the assessment of the situation, the question of controls of shelters and assistance to ships. finally, we accept all the amendments which they have tabled and i hope that they will also be accepted by the council, which would allow us not to have to go to conciliation. we shall shortly be presenting the final measure we need to complete this package which will make it possible to improve safety in maritime transport considerably. after the commission has approved the measures on passenger transport, we will present the measures on crews, which are the human element and always a decisive factor. the rapporteur. - mr president, i think i can begin by saying that i am satisfied with this report, because it represents the end of a long work of the committee on legal affairs and the internal market, which i had the honour of chairing for a significant part of this journey, as well as being the rapporteur for this report. we are presenting today the european parliament's report on the community patent. i should first of all like to say that in this case the european parliament has a simple reporting power. this is the first - i will not say anomaly - but, finally, the first point which i would like to highlight from the point of view of parliament. we are faced with a proposal from the european commission dating from august 2000 - a long time ago, therefore - which was taken up by the lisbon european council, which stressed the importance of obtaining a community patent before the end of 2001; this importance was again highlighted at the barcelona european council, thus urging the council to adopt a political position at the internal market council on 21 may. these facts mark the beginning of a debate which has been difficult, because the adoption of this community patent is not a trivial matter. we are on our second attempt and i hope and trust that this time we will have a community patent. we need a community patent covering the territory of the union, complementary to the european patent and national patents and competitive in the world. these are the three axes which the european commission has taken as a basis of reference and which the committee on legal affairs has taken as a starting point. but for us, mr president, and especially because we have only a simple report, it was essential to reach a consensus in the committee on legal affairs. i think we've reached it. i hope that tomorrow's vote in the house will basically support the position of the committee on legal affairs, which is a position we have reached after many hours of debate and discussion on the following three fundamental points which are the three pillars of this community patent: first, the role of the national offices: there is no doubt that when we have the community patent, the role of the national offices will be very much reduced, unless we give them a complementary job. the report of the committee on legal affairs provides for the possibility of national offices participating in the first stage of the community patent procedure - the search stage - provided that they guarantee a sufficient level of quality. that is the first point of agreement of the committee on legal affairs. secondly, the question of jurisdiction: the commission's proposal is an ambitious one which, incidentally, at present has no legal basis in the treaty, and which would be based on a provision of the treaty of nice which has not yet entered into force, namely the introduction of a centralised community court at first instance. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. thirdly, the languages of the proceedings: at present the commission's proposal is to maintain the european patent system, i.e. three languages of the proceedings (english, french and german). as rapporteur and in view of the fact that english is much more than the language of a member state of the european union, which is the lingua franca of research, i proposed only english. in the end, for reasons of cultural and linguistic plurality, which parliament defends, we have reached a consensus in defending the alicante system, that is, five procedural languages. i think that here too parliament is giving an important political signal which should make the council reflect in order to find a consensus. i say this in view of the latest news i have of the work of the council group.
- mr president, i would like to join my colleague, mr lehne, in congratulating mrs de palacio on the work she has done in drawing up this report. as mrs de palacio has pointed out, the european parliament has only consultative powers here, and we are really in the hands of the commission and the council. but i think that the european parliament is giving good advice at the moment. firstly, as mrs de palacio has pointed out, with regard to the role of the national patent offices, a community such as ours is important. secondly, as mr lehne said, on the question of jurisdiction. the other day lawyers for large american companies told me that the advantage of the american federal system is that state jurisdictions are generally more favourable to local businesses and consumers, while large companies prefer to go to federal jurisdiction, which is more favourable to them. we will probably have to consider whether the attribution of jurisdiction to a special community court might not create an imbalance and also lead to what the americans call forum shopping, whereby each lawyer or legal expert takes the case to the court which is most favourable to him. i would like to mention another aspect, namely that we have arrived at this new european patent by the indirect route of accession to an existing international convention. this raises problems, notably linguistic problems, which are of considerable importance to the european union. the european community is not a federal union, but is approaching a kind of confederation, in which national cultures and traditions are of great importance. in concrete terms, for a country like spain and for the 500 million people who speak spanish, the submission to a language other than their own is going to be a very important limitation on the development of research, not only in our country, but in all the countries that have relied on the spanish patent office to patent inventions. the european parliament can only make a recommendation, through recital 2, with regard to article 5. as mrs de palacio points out, it is recommended to use the alicante system, which has already worked and is working well at the moment with five languages, which allows for a large community participation and at the same time is not expensive. we are seeing that this system is well adapted to the requirements of the european union. i think that parliament's proposals and the agreement we have reached in the committee on legal affairs are reasonable. our group will therefore support all the amendments adopted by the committee on legal affairs, although we do not think it appropriate at this stage to vote on any of the other amendments, as this would upset the balance we have achieved in the committee on legal affairs.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i should like to begin by thanking all the groups for their attitude, which i have already expressed in committee and which has been a constant in the preparation of this sitting. i should also like to mention the cooperation and dialogue we have been able to maintain with the commission and the council, following on from the unanimous approval of this report by the 49 members of the committee on foreign affairs, human rights, common security and defence policy. i now come to the comments on the amendments. firstly, mrs boudjenah has tabled seven amendments, of which i understand that amendments nos 4, 6, 7 and 8 have been withdrawn and that she maintains amendments nos 3, 5 and 9. i would say to mrs boudjenah, first of all, that i think amendment no 5 on the harmonization legislation on immigration is well justified in paragraphs 45 and 46 and that the issue of external debt is adequately dealt with in paragraph 29. i would therefore maintain my position against these amendments. on the other hand, i think amendment no 3 on public services is positive and enriches the report. i would therefore be in favour, although i would suggest that in your vote we should not consider the place raised by the amendment, but paragraph 26a as the appropriate place. i think that amendment no 2 by mrs napoletano is a very positive contribution, since the euroscola programme is a youth programme that works and i am therefore in favour of it. as regards amendment no 1, which i tabled as rapporteur, i think everyone will agree that it makes perfect sense to include the security council resolutions in the report. i am referring, of course, to resolutions 1397 and 1402. finally, i think that amendment no 10 by mrs napoletano on the euro-mediterranean bank is the one that needs further comment. i believe - and the foreign affairs committee feels so - that the current wording is a strong endorsement of the establishment of the bank. the barcelona european council, however, set out positions and measures which, although not in this direction, are not in contradiction with the possibility that we will be considering the bank within a year. i therefore sincerely believe that the group of the party of european socialists has made an effort to synthesise which could be valid for debate in various groups - my own - and that the amendment it proposes is a positive summary of the situation, since we could maintain a consensus not to give up the bank and to support the commission in presenting a new proposal which, of course, should be widely debated in this parliament. i therefore express my support for amendment no 10. i also propose, mr president, a reordering of four paragraphs. in particular, i think that paragraphs 31, 32, 33 and 34 would be more orderly in their expression if they were in order 33, 32, 34 and 31. i also think that paragraph 52, which is purely economic, should be included in it and not in the way it is now. i think it should be placed after paragraph 22. in conclusion, i think that the important thing about this report, and i will not go into details, is two things: firstly, that it should help and guide the valencia conference in the direction of a priority for a euro-mediterranean policy and in the direction of efficiency. i think that is the case and i hope that the vote will reflect that in our part of the debate. secondly, i am thinking of the very serious conflict in the middle east, of the debate we had yesterday, of the sad news we are hearing today from haifa, of the meeting we are having today in madrid, where we hope that a common position can be reached. in view of all this, i think we can say that the barcelona process calls for positive action for stability and peace in general in the region and the middle east. let me remind you that if the valencia meeting takes place as planned, it will be the only forum where the delegations of palestine and israel will be able to be present. i sincerely believe that the instrument we have as the european union with the barcelona process is, if not the most important, probably one of the most important for dialogue and cooperation. it is also a process that is within our reach, because it is our responsibility. i think that you should continue to do your job - and do it seriously. we hope that this will be the case and i therefore thank you, mr president, for the way in which this report has been drawn up and negotiated.

and it should be remembered that there is no military invasion of palestine in israel. otherwise, i believe that this conflict will paralyse and undermine the hopes that have been placed in the development of the european union in this area. we must also remember another conflict that is brewing, but which can erupt at any time, and that is the one in western sahara. it is essential - as we have always said - to recognise the resolutions of the united nations council so that the referendum on self-determination can be held and we can eliminate a possible conflict in the typical task of preventing problems which the european union has set itself. it is also necessary to make it quite clear, as has already been said, that the need to restore respect for democracy and human rights in several countries in the region is affecting this prospect. another aspect which is also worrying is the paradox that if investments are made in this area without respecting the necessary balance, the unexpected effect is to increase unemployment, to displace farmers from the land to the cities where they cannot find work and thus to encourage emigration, whether illegal or not. so we should consider these important aspects. i think that the proposal to develop a partnership model for this area similar to that of the european union, in which we can intervene, is positive, but it should be done with more emphasis and urgency. i therefore also recognize the importance of the latest proposal by the parliamentary assembly, which is crucial for the development of this area.
